results.title: The power and simplicity of propagating errors with Monte Carlo simulations | Towards Data Science
results.content: To demonstrate the application of Monte Carlo simulations for error propagation, let’s consider a very simple subtraction operation **a – b** where both **a** and **b** have some associated uncertainties **da** and **db**. In this example, the uncertainty is propagated both analytically and with a Monte Carlo procedure, to then compare their results. As you see, both the result of the calculation and the error expected from analytical propagation (2.2361) are reasonably converged through iterations of the Monte Carlo procedure. Now, let’s delve into more practical examples where we apply Monte Carlo simulations to estimate the uncertainties of parameters obtained by fitting data. The uncertainties obtained from Monte Carlo simulations (standard deviations) are consistent with the standard errors provided by **fitlm**, confirming the accuracy of the Monte Carlo method for propagating errors in the fitting parameters. results.title: Latin Hypercube Sampling vs. Monte Carlo Sampling | Analytica
results.content: In a post on LinkedIn, David Vose argues that the advantages of Latin Hypercube sampling (LHS) over Monte Carlo are so minimal that “LHS does not deserve a place in modern simulation software.” [1]  He makes some interesting points, yet products like Analytica and Crystal Ball still provide LHS and even offer it as their default method. And I’ve concluded that *yes* —it does make sense to keep Latin Hypercube as the default method. (Feel free to skip this if you already understand Monte Carlo and LHS.) Monte Carlo (MC) simulation generates a random sample of *N* points for each uncertain input variable of a model. It generates a sample of *N* values or scenarios for each result variable in the model using each of the of the corresponding *N* points for each uncertain input. Consider this example: I generated a sample of N=100 points from a standard Normal(0,1) distribution using each method and computed the sample mean.
